summary: In Greek mythology, Talaemenes (Ancient Greek Ταλαημένης) was father of the Maeonian captains Mesthles and Antiphus by a Gygaean nymph. His sons lead the Maeonians — Lydian people of the Tmolus country — in Homer's Catalogue of Ships and in Apollodorus' list of Trojan allies.

sections.heading: Father of the Maeonian captains
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 2.864–866) sets Mesthles and Antiphus, sons of Talaemenes born of the Gygaean lake-nymph, at the head of the Maeonians whose birth was beneath Tmolus. Apollodorus (Epitome 3.35) repeats the patronymic among the allies who join Troy after nine years of siege. Talaemenes himself does not appear as a fighter on stage — only as the named father of the Maeonian command.
